historical_reviews.deepseek: Recognizes a state-changing ForceOff but substitutes a System action for the source Chassis action without vendor authority and omits the source's chassis readback.
historical_reviews.gpt_v2: Correctly preserves Chassis/DGX as the candidate source path while requiring the firmware-specific contract before execution.
historical_reviews.history: No earlier exact source identity record exists.
historical_reviews.v3_1: Chassis.Reset and ComputerSystem.Reset are not interchangeable by assumption: they may expose different allowable ResetType values or affect different resource scopes. The action target and the readback resource must be proven to describe the same physical power domain before approval.

original_test_intent: Verify that one authorized isolated physical chassis becomes off after exactly one vendor-supported Chassis.Reset ForceOff action and that the corresponding chassis resource plus an independent power observer agree on the result.
original_method: Discover and identify the target chassis resource, prove its relationship to the intended SUT and power domain, validate the firmware-supported ForceOff action/readback fields, record workload/filesystem/storage safety, obtain immediate approval, issue one secure POST, independently verify off state, and preserve all logs without retry or recovery power action.
manual_activity: The chassis/workload owner confirms the exact physical power domain, accepts abrupt interruption risk, verifies workload/storage safety, explicitly approves ForceOff and owns any separately authorized recovery or power-on.
required_inputs: Canonical Chassis/DGX resource or discovered replacement
safety_requirements: Never use hardcoded or default credentials
Never expose secrets in URLs or command history
Do not use unapproved TLS bypass
Do not substitute System.Reset without vendor proof
engineer_actions: Approve chassis identity and abrupt-power objective

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: Its System.Reset ForceOff may be valid on some firmware but does not implement the source Chassis/DGX action and lacks the specified chassis-resource readback; it cannot replace the source without an approved mapping.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: After vendor discovery confirms the exact chassis resource and owner approval, POST one `ResetType: ForceOff` to its supported Chassis.Reset action using trusted TLS and protected secrets; verify the same power domain is off through the authoritative chassis field and independent IPMI/console evidence.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: The chassis ForceOff intent and 10/20-minute window remain; default credentials, generic log clearing, System endpoint substitution and automatic recovery are excluded.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Persist the Redfish resource graph linking Chassis, ComputerSystem and physical asset, then capture one action/task plus synchronized chassis-field and independent power observations.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Adds resource-scope proof, workload authorization and ambiguity control around a credential-unsafe destructive command.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: An HTTP success or a System-only status cannot prove the intended chassis/power domain was acted on or that the source Chassis endpoint semantics were honored.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Abrupt chassis power removal can corrupt active storage and lose data. Evidence retention cannot roll back the interruption; recovery remains owner-controlled.

project_override_considerations: The Project must approve whether `/Chassis/DGX/Actions/Chassis.Reset` is authoritative on this firmware and which field proves off state. If only ComputerSystem.Reset is supported, the mapping and equivalence must be explicitly documented before execution.
expected_evidence: BMC/SUT/chassis identity and Redfish resource/power-domain graph
Firmware action contract, allowable ForceOff value and authoritative readback field
Initial power/workload/filesystem/storage safety and explicit approval
Trusted TLS/auth/client metadata with secrets redacted
Complete POST response/task and exactly-one-command audit
Chassis field plus independent off-state timeline, preserved logs, recovery handoff and engineer verdict

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: Items, Chassis.Reset procedure and ForceOff criterion consistently target abrupt chassis power-off. DeepSeek's System endpoint substitution is a reference-review mismatch, not competing Master source content.

blocked_analysis.analysis: The exact chassis resource/action/readback contract and power-domain map are identifiable vendor/project inputs. Execution becomes BLOCKED if they or abrupt-power authorization remain unavailable after the normal request.

review_improvement: Prevents an unapproved System-versus-Chassis substitution and binds the destructive action to a verified physical power domain with independent off-state proof.
independent_technical_reasoning: Redfish resources model scope, not just alternate URLs. A Chassis action can represent enclosure power while a ComputerSystem action represents a logical host; even when both accept ForceOff, their affected hardware and readback may differ. Safe execution therefore requires a proven resource graph and same-domain observation before interpreting completion.
